item.title: Tour: A Closer Look at "Care and Concern" — Fri Oct 16, 1:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:
Join Ackland educators for a lively half-hour look at a small handful of artworks in Care and Concern: Recent Acquisitions of Modern and Contemporary Art. These engaging conversational tours offer a closer look at and new perspectives on works on view at the Museum. Free, but space is limited to 20 participants; first come, first served. This event is part of UNC–Chapel Hill’s Campus Life Experience (CLE) program. Students who attend can scan the QR code provided at the event to receive CLE credit.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: JENNY BLAZING: CAROLINA, OR THEREABOUTS — Sat Oct 17, 1:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description: 5 Points Gallery is pleased to present Carolina, or Thereabouts, a new exhibition of mixed-media paintings by Featured Artist Jenny Blazing exploring the shifting nature of place through observation, memory, and imagination. Grounded in Blazing’s experiences of Carolina, the layered works draw from travel, accumulated visual memories, and unexpected connections that emerge as the paintings evolve to create landscapes that feel familiar without belonging to any single geography. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our ten Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, October 16, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artist. Carolina, or Thereabouts runs from October 15 through November 14, 2026. item.title: Maybe Happy Ending — Sat Oct 17, 2:00 PM — DPAC Presented by First Horizon
item.description:
Tony Award Winner! Best Musical Winner of 6 Tony Awards, including Best Musical, MAYBE HAPPY ENDING tells the deeply human story of a chance encounter that sparks connection, adventure, and maybe even love. Helmed by Tony Award-winning director Michael Arden (Parade), MAYBE HAPPY ENDING has been called “one of the best musicals in years” (USA Today) and even “The best musical in eons!” (Observer). Don’t miss the totally original new musical adventure that explores what it means to be human. Even if they’re not.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Fate & Folklore's Samhain Market at Zeitgeist — Sat Oct 17, 6:00 PM — Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar
item.description:
Join Fate & Folklore fora. Samhain to remember! Mid October you’ll find us hosting a night market from 6pm-10pm at Zeitgeist Bar with Hatch Burritos and Night School Bar. There will be state fair inspired food, limited edition cocktails, a bone thrower, and of course our local vendors. Night school bar will be hosting an hour long informational talk and discussion of the significance of witches in our every day lives and modern practices. We couldn’t be more excited for this collaboration. Come find the community and witchy discussion you’ve been looking for this Samhain October 17th.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Aloreing Destinations: Tickets Please! — Sat Oct 17, 7:00 PM — American Tobacco Campus
item.description:
Join the Museum of Durham History and the Ghost Guild at 7:00 p.m. in the Fullsteam Theater at the American Tobacco Campus for Aloreing Destinations: Tickets Please! a spooky evening where we will explore some of North Carolina’s most historic and reportedly haunted performance venues, including Durham’s Carolina Theatre. Drawing on The Ghost Guild’s research and investigation work, the presentation will explore stories of tragic backstage legends, unexplained occurrences, and the traditions that have kept ghost stories alive in theaters long after the final curtain. Doors open with complimentary appetizers and a cash bar in the Stoker Club, located at the Fullsteam Theater. Following the event there will be a Q&A and mingling with The Ghost Guild team and fellow history and paranormal enthusiasts in Lucky’s Den/Fullsteam Public House. Admission is free, but you must reserve a ticket in advance below.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Crank Arm Karaoke — Sat Oct 17, 7:00 PM — Crank Arm Brewing Co.
item.description:

item.title: Frightful Folk Tales at Vance Birthplace — Sat Oct 17, 7:00 PM — Governor Zebulon B. Vance Birthplace
item.description:
Join us at Vance Birthplace on Saturday, Oct. 17 to get into the spirit of Halloween with spooky stories from Appalachia and beyond! Dr. Delanna Reed, professor emerita of Storytelling at East Tennessee State University, will bring these tales to life through spoken word from 7pm to 8pm. Visitors are welcome to bring a blanket or chair, and as the sun sets, they can take a seat around our campfire. These stories are suitable for ages 12 and up.
This event is free and does not require registration in advance, but donations are encouraged. If you have any questions, please reach out via email at vance@dncr.nc.gov or by phone at (828) 645-6706!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Duke Arts Presents: Falling: a disabled love story — Sat Oct 17, 7:30 PM — Rubenstein Arts Center
item.description:
Aaron Pang walks with a cane, and everyone asks "what happened?" He's tired of answering and so he wrote a solo show to tell it in one go. One accident, two stories: one you've heard a thousand times, one you've never heard before.
Falling is an uncomfortably sexy and hilariously vulnerable stumble through Aaron's misadventures searching for love, lust, and life after disability. Pang is a writer and comedian from Oakland, California whose work blends sincerity and sharp humor to challenge familiar narratives about disabled bodies and relationships.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Oct 17, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

Join us this fall for Exploring Membership, a three-session opportunity to get to know one another, learn more about the Congregation and our relationship with Duke Chapel, explore the faith and practices that shape our life together, and consider what it means to belong and participate in this community.

item.title: The Roxelanne Effekt — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Carolina Theatre of Durham
item.description: POWER AND NOSTALGIA HAVE A SOUND. This is your chance to listen to select movements from Haydn’s Symphonies No. 47, 63, 73, and 103 paired with the nostalgic call of Mozart’s Posthorn Serenade. Experience the wit, elegance, and imagination of Joseph Haydn through a captivating selection of movements drawn from several of his most beloved symphonies. This unique program highlights Haydn’s remarkable creativity while revealing how even he was not above borrowing from himself, revisiting and reimagining some of his most charming and effective musical ideas. Named for its celebrated posthorn solo, which echoes the call of a traveling mail coach, Mozart’s Posthorn Serenade transports listeners to a world of elegance and festivity. One of Mozart’s most joyful and expansive works, it captures the spirit of celebration and adventure that characterized the young composer at the height of his creative powers. item.description:

Duke Chapel's Choral Evensong follows this historic pattern, using the liturgy of the Book of Common Prayer and featuring choral and organ music from the English cathedral tradition, led by the Chapel's Evensong Singers.

item.title: An Evening with Haviv Rettig Gur — Sun Oct 18, 6:00 PM — TBA
item.description:
Jewish Life at Duke presents an evening with journalist and political analyst Haviv Rettig Gur. Haviv Rettig Gur is an Israeli journalist, host of the "Ask Haviv Anything" podcast, Middle East analyst at "The Free Press," and senior analyst at "The Times of Israel."
Rettig Gur has covered Israel's politics, foreign policy, education system and relationship with the Jewish diaspora since 2005, reported from over 20 countries, served as director of communications for the Jewish Agency for Israel, Israel's largest NGO, and taught at prestigious pre-military academies.
Not open to the general public. This event is ticketed and by-invitation.
Tickets are limited. Current students can request a ticket by filling out the following request form: https://duke.is/HRG

item.title: CEE Seminar - Environmental Relevance in Disinfection Research? Influence of Species, Conformation, and “Lived Experience” on Decay Kinetics of Microbial Contaminants — Mon Oct 19, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: Species/strain diversity (i.e., identity determined by genetics) and physiology or conformation (i.e., functional/physical state determined by "lived experience") have the potential to influence the inactivation or decay kinetics of microbial contaminants, such as bacteria or DNA. Nonetheless, most disinfection research utilizes reference strain organisms or model systems cultivated in the laboratory for experiments used to assess disinfection kinetics, with limited discussion of the environmental relevance of the observed disinfection behavior. To illustrate the importance of identity and lived experience on disinfection kinetics, two examples from research in the Silverman Laboratory will be presented. The first is an evaluation of divergent inactivation kinetics of wastewater-sourced E. coli and enterococci, laboratory-cultured E. coli and three species of Enterococcus with exposure to commonly used disinfectants (i.e., free chlorine, monochloramine, UVC, and simulated sunlight). item.description:

item.title: Ari Joskowicz: "Money and Memory: How Funding Shaped the Documentation of Jewish History and the Holocaust" — Mon Oct 19, 5:00 PM — Gray 229
item.description:
The Sperling Center for Jewish Studies welcomes Ari Joskowicz, who will give a lecture entitled "Money and Memory: How Funding Shaped the Documentation of Jewish History and the Holocaust." Joskowicz is the Eugene Greener Jr. Chair in Jewish Studies and Professor of Jewish Studies and History at Vanderbilt University, where he also directs the Max Kade Center for European and German Studies. A historian of modern Jewish and European history, his scholarship explores the intersections of Jewish history, minority politics, memory, and the Holocaust, with particular attention to the relationships between Jewish and Romani communities in Europe.
Joskowicz is the author of the award-winning books Rain of Ash: Roma, Jews, and the Holocaust (Princeton University Press, 2023) and The Modernity of Others: Jewish Anti-Catholicism in Germany and France (Stanford University Press, 2014). His research has been recognized with major honors, including the Ernst Fraenkel Prize of the Wiener Library

item.title: Artist Talk: Kiran Masroor — Mon Oct 19, 5:30 PM — Duke Chapel
item.description:
Duke medical student Kiran Masroor, selected as this year's C. Eric Lincoln Theology and Arts Fellow, will give a talk on her exhibition "Sacred are the waters."
Free admission.
On display in Duke Chapel from October 2 through November 5, "Sacred are the waters" presents thirteen poems framed individually but all part of one mythological cosmology. They interweave themes of life and death, building to a climactic section that expresses that tension in ecstatic release.
Masroor is displaying her cycle of original poems as this year's recipient of the C. Eric Lincoln Theology and Arts Fellowship, which provides funding for a Duke student to complete a sacred art project and display it in the Chapel. Her poetry has been published in VOICES Magazine, Muzzle Magazine, the Yale Daily News, and the anthology Without a Doubt: poems illuminating faith. Her poem "Interrupted Connection" received second place in the forty-fourth annual William Carlos William poetry competition.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Jan 14 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Thu Jan 14, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources
